title.narrative: Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) for the IDPs in WN

description.narrative: Since the conflict occurred in Khartoum on 15th April 2024, the Situation of internally displaced people (IDPs) who fled clashes between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sennar state, re-emerged after the conflict erupted on 26th June 2024 in Jebel Moya village, Sennar and spread to Sinjar locality which has resulted in the displacement of over 136,000 individuals. An estimated 7,333 IDPs, mostly from Jabal Moya and Al Dali, fled to Al Jabalain and different localities fled to White Nile state. This represents the second or third displacement since the beginning of the war, after having fled Khartoum in the first months of the war and Al Jazira state in December 2023. Malnutrition among children and some adults, especially the elderly and lactating mothers among the displaced persons in Kosti is high and is increasing as new displacements and arrivals continue. Kosti supply routes from Khartoum, Jezira, Gedaref and Red Sea states are all closed due to the fighting further exacerbating the nutritional challenges among the displaced people and the host communities. A rapid assessment of the displaced people has yet to be done to ascertain the severity of the problem among children who are the most affected and those in other categories. Hunger in the camps is evident as the displaced people go without food due to a lack of food provisions. Host community members are also experiencing similar circumstances due to road blockades, high inflation, a lack of jobs to earn a living, and ongoing floods.
